name: blockhash
why: Perceptual image hashing shows how pictures can be reduced to comparable fingerprints, a neat idea if you dig in.

brief.what_it_is: blockhash is a command-line tool that computes perceptual hashes of images. You pass it one or more image files, and it prints a hash for each, computed with the block mean value method. Similar-looking images should produce similar hashes, so you can compare pictures by their fingerprints rather than their bytes. It is written in C and uses ImageMagick's libmagickwand to read images.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no separate problem statement. It says the tool implements the algorithm from 'Block Mean Value Based Image Perceptual Hashing' by Bian Yang, Fan Gu and Xiamu Niu, and it comes from Commons Machinery.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It names the algorithm, Block Mean Value Based Image Perceptual Hashing, and points to the paper by its authors. Anyone who wants the mechanism will need the paper or the source code.

commands_seen.context: Installs the ImageMagick development headers the build needs on Debian/Ubuntu.
Installs the same ImageMagick development headers on Fedora and related distros.
Configures the build from the source directory; the project uses the waf build system.
Builds blockhash; the binary lands in ./build.
Calculates hashes for the given image files.

brief.install_notes: Requires libmagickwand, installed as the ImageMagick development package (libmagickwand-dev on Debian/Ubuntu, ImageMagick-devel on Fedora). Build from source with ./waf configure and ./waf, then optionally ./waf install. The README does not mention Homebrew; the brew entry lists the executable as blockhash.
brief.standout: The tool implements a specific published perceptual hashing paper rather than a generic average hash. It is a small, single-purpose C program with few dependencies beyond ImageMagick.
brief.status: unknown. The README shows a test CI badge and a 2014 copyright line, but it gives no release version, date, or changelog, and I did not check the commit history. The README reads like a finished, small tool, but I cannot confirm it is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: Building needs ImageMagick development headers, and the build uses the waf toolchain rather than a standard make or cmake step. The README does not describe output format, how to compare hashes, or supported image types beyond what ImageMagick reads. The copyright line dates from 2014. The brew description says only 'Perceptual image hash calculation tool'.
quotes: This is a perceptual image hash calculation tool based on algorithm descibed in Block Mean Value Based Image Perceptual Hashing by Bian Yang, Fan Gu and Xiamu Niu.
Run `blockhash [list of images]` for calculating hashes.
